note: Range from the middle out: a hum held in the middle of the voice, a lip roll held on one note a semitone lower each round, then one slide down through the middle. Each block has its own feel or fix line, the controls are the tools' Start and Restart, and the one care line sits on the slide. No key or tempo to move. missing: a lip-roll shape that stays in the middle of the voice (every slide of the tool crosses both breaks, and "hold" sits in chest voice).

exercise.title: Lip rolls through the middle of your voice
exercise.why: A lip roll only keeps buzzing while your air is steady and your throat is loose, so the buzz tells you when you start to push, and the middle of your voice is where it is easiest to keep.

cells.text:
Press Start below: a note plays first, then the mic starts. Hum an easy note near it, and keep the ball in the valley between the two marks until the ring fills. Take a breath before the next hold.
Practice until the hum is as quiet at the end of a hold as at the start.

cells.heading: A lip roll on one note

cells.text:
Press Start below to begin the rounds: the mic starts with it. A tone plays one note first. Then lip roll the same note on your own, lips loose and buzzing, while your line draws over the tone's path. Each round is a semitone lower.
If the buzz stops, breathe in and start the note again with less air.
When the rounds are done, press Restart below to go again.

Press Start below to begin the rounds: the mic starts with it. The tone slides from high to low and plays the whole time. Lip roll along with it, and keep the buzz even as the slide passes through the middle of your voice.
Practice until the buzz stays even all the way down: here that matters more than an exact note.
_Don't reach for high notes: join the slide where the buzz comes easily._
